newsitem.title: USA: U.S. inflation tame but Fed must look ahead - Rivlin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. inflation tame but Fed must look ahead - Rivlin.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin on Thursday said U.S. inflation appeared to be contained for the time being, but emphasized that the central bank needed to look ahead.
"We've seen a strong economy with moderate wage increases and so far no real evidence of acceleration of inflation but the real question is, how long will this go on?" Rivlin said.
"The Federal Reserve has to look at what might be happening a few months out," she added.
Earlier, in testimony to the Joint Economic Committee of Congress, Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan made similar remarks about the need for the Fed to be forward-looking.
Rivlin said there was "some mystery" as to why inflation had not picked up so far.

"With this tight labor market, we would have expected a more rapid increase in wages and more pass-through of wage increase into prices," Rivlin said, adding that it was also a mystery as to whether the unexpected relationship between labor markets and inflation would continue.
Rivlin, who was addressing reporters after delivering a lecture in Lincoln, Neb., was also asked about proposals to deal with the perceived overstatement of the Consumer Price Index.
Greenspan has suggested that Congress name a commission that would set cost-of-living increases for federal benefits and taxes, taking into account of the bias.
Rivlin, however, said she did not think such a panel was necessary, adding that it might make more sense for Congress to legislate a temporary adjustment for the CPI.

"It ought to be temporary and have a sunset for a defined period of years, maybe five years," Rivlin said. During that time, she said Congress could assess the effects of technical changes to the index that the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics is putting into effect.
